--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.local_reaching_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Calculate the local reaching centrality of every node. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.local_reaching_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Calculate the local reaching centrality of every node. title: >- [Graph.local_reaching_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Calculate the local reaching centrality of every node. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate the local reaching centrality of every node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L62716-L62857){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.local_reaching_centrality( weighted=None, normalized=True, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Local reaching centrality](../assets/graphs/local-reaching-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A five-node directed out-tree, like an org chart: A heads B and C, and B heads D and E. Each node is shaded by the share of the other four nodes it can reach. A reaches all of them and scores 1.00, B reaches D and E for 0.50, and the leaves C, D and E reach no one and score 0." width="100%"} Local reaching centrality (Mones, Vicsek & Vicsek, 2012) measures how much of the network a node can reach, and how easily: - on an unweighted directed graph, it is the share of other nodes reachable from the node, which separates sources at the top of a hierarchy from sinks at the bottom - on an unweighted undirected graph, it averages `1 / distance` over all other nodes (unreachable ones count 0), like a normalized harmonic centrality - on a weighted graph, it averages the mean edge weight along the strongest path to each reachable node, where strong edges count as short (distance = total weight / weight) It is the building block of `global_reaching_centrality()`, which measures how hierarchical the whole network is. Values match NetworkX, which computes one node at a time. With weights, if several equally strong paths reach a node, their mean weights can differ, and the two libraries may pick different ones. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. Weights must be positive. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : With weights, divide by the mean edge weight so scores are comparable across graphs. Default is `True`. Ignored without weights. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store scores in. If `None` (default), uses `"local_reaching_centrality"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph has fewer than two nodes or no edges, or a weight is not positive. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~global_reaching_centrality`) : Summarize the scores as one hierarchy score. [](`~harmonic_centrality`) : Equal up to scale on undirected, unweighted graphs. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a reporting tree, the head of the organization reaches everyone and each leaf reaches no one: ::: {#af1cfd6d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec org = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("ceo", "cto"), ("ceo", "cfo"), ("cto", "dev1"), ("cto", "dev2")], directed=True, ) org.local_reaching_centrality().get_node_df().select( "label", "local_reaching_centrality" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
shape: (5, 2)
labellocal_reaching_centrality
strf64
"ceo"1.0
"cto"0.5
"cfo"0.0
"dev1"0.0
"dev2"0.0
``` ::: ::: ### Courses that open doors In `courses()`, each edge points from a prerequisite to a course that requires it, so a course's local reaching centrality is the share of the other courses that need it, directly or through a chain of prerequisites, stored here as `"reach"`. Introduction to Programming (CS101) leads to 11 of the other 16, and Data Structures (CS102) to 10: ::: {#01683abf .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} courses = ( ec.courses() .local_reaching_centrality(attr_name="reach") .layout_multipartite(subset_key="level") ) ( courses.get_node_df() .select("label", "title", "reach") .sort("reach", descending=True) .head(5) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
shape: (5, 3)
labeltitlereach

"CS101""Introduction to Programming"0.6875
"CS102""Data Structures"0.625
"MATH101""Calculus I"0.375
"MATH102""Calculus II"0.3125

``` ::: ::: With the courses in columns by number, the scores fall from left to right, and the 400-level courses, which lead nowhere, score 0: ::: {#9e5cef19 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} courses.plot(layout="pos", color_by="reach", label_by="label") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### Plants that feed the most In `food_web()`, each edge points from a food to a species that eats it, so a species' local reaching centrality is the share of the other species its energy reaches. The four plants lead, and the Grass and the Oak each feed 7 of the other 15 species, directly or through what eats them: ::: {#4ac0e1bc .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} web = ec.food_web().local_reaching_centrality(attr_name="reach") ( web.get_node_df() .select("label", "kind", "reach") .sort("reach", descending=True) .head(4) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#05b9c8a2 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} web.plot(layout="pos", color_by="reach", label_by="label", height=360) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Summing up how far every node falls short of the top score gives `global_reaching_centrality()`. [Centrality](../user-guide/centrality.qmd#more-measures) sets it beside the other centrality measures, with what each one measures.
